svg.title: What onetree land does before a branch moves
svg.desc: Animated diagram of a onetree landing. A candidate commit built from a session's private index passes four steps in order (claims audit, payload gate, test referee, compare-and-swap) before it becomes a commit on the branch main. One candidate with an unclaimed path is refused at the audit, and of two racing candidates one wins and the other is rebuilt and tried again. The animation has five steps. Step 1: onetree land builds a candidate commit from the session's private index. The shared index and the working tree are not touched. A row of boxes runs from left to right: a session with its private index, four numbered steps (claims audit, payload gate, test referee, compare-and-swap) and the branch main. A rail connects them. A token marked A, the candidate commit of Agent A, appears at the session's index. Step 2: Each step can refuse. Only a candidate that passes all four moves the ref. A landing is recorded in the append-only log as an intent and a landed event. The token A moves along the rail and stops at each step. Each step turns green as the candidate passes it: the claims audit, the payload gate, the test referee (shown working for a moment before it turns green) and the compare-and-swap. The token then moves onto the branch main and becomes a new commit marked A. Step 3: If one changed path was not claimed by this session, the whole candidate is refused. Nothing reaches the branch. A token marked B starts from the index. The index now lists a second file, src/db.py, marked "not claimed". The token stops at the first step, the claims audit, which turns red and shows the reason unclaimed_paths. The token is crossed out and disappears. The branch main is unchanged. Step 4: When two landings race, the compare-and-swap lets exactly one move the ref. The other is rebuilt on the new head and goes through the steps again. Two tokens, C and B, travel through the first three steps one behind the other. At the compare-and-swap, C arrives first and becomes a new commit on main. For B the step turns amber: the head has moved. B travels back along a dashed return line labelled "moved head: rebuilt on the new head, tried again", passes all four steps again and becomes the next commit on main, after C. Step 5: Every commit on the branch is the exact candidate that was audited, gated and tested. A refused candidate leaves the branch where it was. The final picture: all four steps are green and the branch main carries three new commits in the order A, C, B, after the commit it started with.

g.text: 1 · A candidate is built from the private index
onetree land builds a candidate commit from the session's private index.
The shared index and the working tree are not touched.
2 · Four steps before the branch moves
Each step can refuse. Only a candidate that passes all four moves the ref.
A landing is recorded in the append-only log as an intent and a landed event.
3 · One unclaimed path refuses it all
If one changed path was not claimed by this session,
the whole candidate is refused. Nothing reaches the branch.
4 · A race has exactly one winner
When two landings race, the compare-and-swap lets exactly one move the ref.
The other is rebuilt on the new head and goes through the steps again.
5 · What reaches the branch
Every commit on the branch is the exact candidate that was audited, gated and tested.
A refused candidate leaves the branch where it was.
